news.title: Diesel price declines picking up pace
news.summary: The national average for retail diesel posted its fourth weekly decline in a row, falling about 24 cents to roughly $5.70 a gallon, though it remains well above early-March levels.
news.why: Shippers should check that carrier fuel surcharges are stepping down weekly in line with the DOE benchmark instead of lagging the drop.

news.title: RICO Lawsuit: Are Major Freight Brokers Manipulating the Market?
news.summary: A group of trucking firms has filed a civil racketeering suit accusing two of the largest U.S. freight brokers of steering rates down through low-cost carriers, with a trial not expected before 2028.
news.why: Shippers that route most truckload freight through a few big brokers may want to review rate transparency clauses and carrier-vetting terms while the case plays out.

news.title: EU to Temporarily Cap Hybrid Vehicle Imports from China
news.summary: Starting December 1, the EU will apply 200-day import quotas that roughly halve expected Chinese hybrid-car volumes, with separate caps for Japan, the UK, Turkey and South Korea.
news.why: Auto importers and dealers in Europe should lock in quota allocations early and plan for tighter supply and higher landed costs on hybrids into mid-2027.

news.title: Trump Admin Expected to Raise Tariffs Against Dozens of Nations
news.summary: The U.S. Trade Representative is reportedly about to publish findings from an unfair-trade probe covering China, the EU and more than a dozen other economies, likely opening the door to higher tariffs.
news.why: Importers should model duty scenarios by origin now, with China facing the steepest likely increase, and consider pulling forward shipments where the math works.

news.title: U.S. Chip Curbs Won't Impact Malaysia's China Ties, PM Says
news.summary: Malaysia's prime minister said new U.S. limits on advanced AI chip shipments will not stop the country from doing business with Chinese companies, while pledging to monitor U.S.-linked firms.
news.why: Electronics buyers sourcing through Malaysian assembly hubs should expect more export-control paperwork and end-use checks on high-end components.

news.title: WSC: uncertain regulations could hinder shipping sector moves to cut greenhouse gases
news.summary: The World Shipping Council is pressing the IMO to adopt binding global emissions rules this month, noting carriers have already ordered more than 1,350 dual-fuel ships.
news.why: Whether a global carbon framework passes will shape future bunker and green surcharges, so ocean shippers should watch the IMO decision before finalizing 2027 contracts.

news.title: Best Buy taps AI platform for supplier insights
news.summary: Best Buy is partnering with Circana on an AI-driven platform intended to give the retailer and its vendors better visibility for planning and assortment decisions.
news.why: Suppliers to big-box retailers should expect more data-sharing requests and be ready to act on shared sell-through insights in replenishment talks.

news.title: Walgreens scales micro-fulfillment strategy with Pennsylvania site
news.summary: Walgreens opened a 68,000-square-foot automated center in Allentown that can fill over 28 million prescriptions a year for about 650 stores.
news.why: Centralized automated filling shows how retailers are shifting labor out of stores, a model worth benchmarking for any multi-site distribution network.

news.title: Tractor Supply boosts same-day delivery options
news.summary: Tractor Supply is widening its same-day delivery services as Amazon pushes deeper into rural markets.
news.why: Rural last-mile is becoming a competitive battleground, so vendors serving farm and ranch retail should prepare for smaller, faster store replenishment cycles.

news.title: Data center boom is driving warehouse and logistics demand, Cushman & Wakefield says
news.summary: Cushman & Wakefield reports that data-center-related industrial leasing hit 50 million square feet through Q3, more than double all of 2025, as AI equipment imports jumped 62%.
news.why: Tenants competing for warehouse space near data-center corridors should expect tighter availability and firmer rents, so renewals deserve early attention.

news.title: Deloitte: More shoppers plan to shop over Thanksgiving holiday, but spending could stay flat
news.summary: A Deloitte survey finds 87% of consumers intend to shop during the Black Friday to Cyber Monday stretch, the highest share since 2016, but expected spending is flat at about $624.
news.why: More shoppers spending the same total points to heavier discounting and smaller baskets, so retailers should watch margin and avoid overbuying replenishment stock.

news.title: U.S. Probes Suspected Iranian Cyberattacks on Up to 50 Ships, WSJ Reports
news.summary: U.S. authorities are investigating whether Iran was behind a string of cyberattacks that hit as many as 50 vessels, many of them energy tankers.
news.why: Cyber risk at sea adds another layer of disruption to Gulf energy routes, so buyers exposed to fuel and petrochemical inputs should keep alternate supply options warm.

news.title: U.S. Targets Financial Networks Behind Iran's Tanker Fleet and Oil Trade
news.summary: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned payment networks that help fund Iran's oil exports and its national tanker company.
news.why: Companies chartering tankers or buying energy cargoes must tighten sanctions screening of counterparties and payment chains to avoid secondary penalties.

news.title: Spain to Ban Ship Scrubber Wastewater Discharges Starting July 2027
news.summary: Spain will prohibit vessels from releasing scrubber washwater in its ports and inland waters from July 1, 2027.
news.why: Carriers relying on open-loop scrubbers may switch to pricier compliant fuel on Spanish calls, which could show up as higher surcharges for Iberian trade lanes.

news.title: Fake Iran Tanker Highlights Uncertainty Around Hormuz Traffic
news.summary: A tanker with no prior history broadcast that it had slipped past the U.S. blockade near the Strait of Hormuz, exposing how hard it is to trust vessel-tracking data there.
news.why: Unreliable AIS signals in the Gulf make shipment ETAs and risk assessments less certain, so importers should build extra buffer into Middle East-linked lead times.
